SDV's GaussianCopula, CTGAN, TVAE and SingleTablePreset synthesizers are run as evaluation subjects in this generator-selection study, one of the candidates (alongside MostlyAI) whose synthetic output is assessed for fidelity and used to test augmentation.

title: Augmenting Insufficiently Accruing Oncology Clinical Trials Using Generative Models: Validation Study
summary: This retrospective validation study evaluates whether generative models can synthesize additional patients to compensate for insufficient accrual in oncology clinical trials, using 10 datasets from 9 completed cancer trials with progressively larger fractions of the latest-recruited patients removed and then simulated back in. Four generative approaches -- sequential synthesis with decision trees, a Bayesian network, a GAN, and a VAE -- were compared against bootstrap resampling using replication metrics (decision agreement, estimate agreement, standardized difference, CI overlap) and fidelity metrics. CTGAN and its tabular VAE variant (TVAE), both described using their per-mode normalization and conditional-vector mechanisms, are two of the four generative models run and benchmarked as evaluation subjects, with sequential synthesis ultimately performing best.

It cites CTGAN as related work in the space of generative approaches for tabular data. No further detail on how CTGAN is used is available from the metadata alone.
evidence: Metadata indicates the paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper; no citing sentence or abstract text was provided beyond this reference.

title: Can Augmentation Help Small Survey Datasets: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Academic Impact of Social Media Addiction and Procrastination
summary: This paper investigates whether synthetic-data augmentation can improve machine-learning prediction of academic risk from social-media addiction and procrastination, using two small, imbalanced student surveys and seven classifiers (LR, RF, GB, SVM, KNN, GNB, MLP). It compares SMOTENC, Gaussian Copula, and CTGAN as augmentation techniques, finding effects are modest and model/dataset dependent. CTGAN and Gaussian Copula, both SDV-family synthesizers, are run as generative augmentation methods and evaluated as two of several oversampling approaches.
evidence: "The third approach used is CTGAN, a generative model that learns the joint distribution of tabular data by capturing complex relationships between continuous and categorical features, enabling the generation of realistic synthetic datasets [26]." Abstract also lists Gaussian Copula (GC) as an augmentation method alongside CTGAN and SMOTENC.

title: Can Synthetic Data be Fair and Private? A Comparative Study of Synthetic Data Generation and Fairness Algorithms
summary: This paper compares five synthetic data generators (CTGAN, DistilGPT2/GReaT, ADSGAN, PATEGAN, DECAF) and several fairness pre-processing algorithms on learning-analytics datasets, evaluating trade-offs between privacy, fairness, and utility. It finds DECAF best balances privacy and fairness but sacrifices utility, and that applying fairness pre-processing to synthetic rather than real data yields greater fairness gains. CTGAN is run as one of the five synthetic data generators evaluated, with its conditional generator and training-by-sampling mechanism described and its outputs measured for fairness, privacy, and downstream AUC-ROC.
evidence: "CTGAN is a GAN-based method designed to model tabular distributions and generate row samples from those distributions. Its unique advantages include the ability to mitigate class imbalances in training data through conditional generators and sampled training [55]."

title: The Cardiologist Driving Synthetic AI: The TIMA Method for Clinically Supervised Synthetic Data Generation
summary: This paper introduces TIMA (Team-Implementation Multidisciplinary Approach), a methodological framework for embedding cardiologists directly into every phase of synthetic clinical data generation, illustrated through cardiology use cases such as atrial fibrillation risk prediction and infective endocarditis mortality estimation. Rather than reporting quantitative performance results, it focuses on iterative clinician-data scientist validation to ensure clinical plausibility and coherence of synthetic datasets. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is named only as an illustrative example of a Python-based framework through which the proposed constraint-based clinical rules could be technically operationalized, not as a system the authors ran or evaluated.

title: Cascade-Based Input-Doubling Classifier for Predicting Survival in Allogeneic Bone Marrow Transplants: Small Data Case
summary: This paper proposes an input-doubling classifier for small-data binary classification in transplantology, using a Probabilistic Neural Network to expand the feature space of an augmented dataset before a second machine learning algorithm performs final classification, with hyperparameters tuned via Dual Annealing. The method is tested on a small allogeneic bone marrow transplant survival dataset and compared against several existing approaches. CTGAN is only cited in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, and is never run or engaged with in the body text.

title: A case study comparing anonymized and synthetic health insurance claims data for medication safety assessments
summary: This paper presents a case study comparing classical data anonymization and synthetic data generation on a small, high-dimensional German health insurance claims dataset, evaluating fidelity, reproducibility of a medication-safety study's hazard-ratio outcomes, and privacy risks under two threat scenarios. The authors used a synthetization approach (associated with co-author affiliation MOSTLY AI) rather than CTGAN, and discuss a separate prior study in which SDV's CTGAN failed to preserve the original study's conclusions, while also citing CTGAN as a more commonly used alternative worth testing in future work. CTGAN is only cited and discussed, never run, in this paper's own experiments.

title: A Case Study Exploring Data Synthesis Strategies on Tabular vs. Aggregated Data Sources for Official Statistics
summary: This case study from Statistics Netherlands investigates generating synthetic microdata from open-source aggregated (macro) data versus traditional micro-level synthesis, proposing three knowledge scenarios (zero, internal, external) built on a Gaussian-copula-based SYNC method, and evaluating utility and privacy risk via matching attacks. As part of the micro-to-micro baseline comparison, the authors run CTGAN alongside CART to synthesize microdata from real tabular records, comparing rule-violation rates, regression MSE, and residual patterns against their macro-to-micro Gaussian copula approach. CTGAN is used as one of two baseline synthesizers benchmarked against the paper's proposed macro-to-micro synthesis strategy, with the sdv.dev toolkit cited as the source of the CTGAN implementation used.
evidence: "We train the model using the CART and CTGAN full synthetic datasets" and footnote citing https://sdv.dev/ as the source used to run CTGAN as a micro-to-micro synthesis baseline compared against the authors' macro-to-micro Gaussian copula approach.

title: CasTGAN: Cascaded Generative Adversarial Network for Realistic Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes CasTGAN, a cascaded GAN architecture for synthesizing realistic tabular data, in which a dedicated generator per feature is used sequentially to better preserve inter-feature dependencies and reduce invalid synthetic records compared to prior tabular GANs. The authors benchmark CasTGAN's classification utility, statistical similarity, and validity against five state-of-the-art tabular GAN baselines across six real-world datasets, and also assess privacy risks from white-box attacks. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of the five baseline generators and compared against CasTGAN on PR-AUC, KS statistics, correlation preservation, and invalid-record rate, with CTGAN's conditional training and mode-specific normalization design discussed in the related work.

title: Causality-Aware Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations
summary: The paper proposes calime, an extension of LIME that replaces LIME's random local sampling with a causality-aware synthetic data generator, gencda, to produce more faithful and causally consistent explanations of black-box classifiers. Experiments compare calime's synthetic neighborhoods against the original data using outlier-detection and statistical fidelity indicators. To assess how well the generated synthetic neighborhood matches the real data, the authors adopt the statistical quality measures (e.g. GMLogLikelihood, KSTest, ContinuousKLDivergence) described in the SDV paper, applying SDV's synthetic-data evaluation methodology as part of their own experimental pipeline.

title: On the causality-preservation capabilities of generative modelling
summary: This paper investigates whether generative models used to produce synthetic tabular data preserve the causal structure of the original data, not just its correlational structure, motivating a path toward causally-valid synthetic data for decision-making. It surveys and describes prior generative approaches to tabular data synthesis, including TGAN and CTGAN, as prior art that addresses multi-modal continuous distributions and imbalanced categorical columns. TGAN and CTGAN are discussed in the related-work section as architectural prior art the authors' causal analysis departs from, but neither is run in the reported experiments.

title: Causality for Tabular Data Synthesis: A High-Order Structure Causal Benchmark Framework
summary: This paper introduces a benchmark framework for evaluating tabular data synthesis models on their ability to preserve high-order, multivariate causal structure rather than just pairwise statistics or downstream task accuracy. The authors generate benchmark datasets from sampled causal graphs, train several state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers on them, and score the resulting synthetic data with causal-discovery-based metrics (structural Hamming distance, skeleton F1, d-separation tests, directionality). CTGAN and TVAE, drawn from the CTGAN paper, are run as two of eight baseline generators (alongside TabSyn, STASY, TabDDPM, CoDi, GReaT, and TabPFN) and are shown to underperform newer diffusion- and transformer-based methods on high-order causal fidelity.

title: Causally Disentangled Generative Variational AutoEncoder
summary: This paper proposes CDG-VAE, a variational autoencoder trained with a supervised regularization scheme that provably yields causally disentangled generation, along with a new metric for measuring causal disentanglement under arbitrary DAG structures. On tabular datasets (loan, adult, covertype) the authors benchmark CDG-VAE against TVAE and CTAB-GAN, and also build 'CDG-TVAE', a hybrid synthesizer that combines TVAE's mode-specific normalization technique with the CDG-VAE architecture to better preserve causal structure while producing high-quality synthetic data. TVAE, introduced in the CTGAN paper, is thus both a comparison baseline and a component whose normalization technique is incorporated into the authors' new model.
evidence: "CDG-TVAE is the new synthesizer where the mode-specific normalization technique of TVAE is combined with CDG-VAE" while TVAE [38] is also run unmodified as a comparison synthesizer in Table 4.

title: Data-Centric AI to Improve Churn Prediction with Synthetic Data
summary: This paper presents a comparative, data-centric study of widely used data synthesis algorithms applied to customer churn prediction, testing strategies of substituting, balancing, and augmenting real training data with synthetic data. It benchmarks these resampling/synthesis strategies to determine which best improves downstream churn classification performance. CTGAN and TVAE are named among the deep generative models evaluated as data synthesis methods in this benchmark.

title: Data-centric AI to Improve Early Detection of Mental Illness
summary: This conference paper argues for a data-centric AI perspective on early mental-illness detection, comparing established tabular data synthesis methods to assess the impact of synthetic data and data augmentation on machine-learning performance for mental health tasks. It positions itself against model-centric AI approaches that only tune model architecture rather than data quality. title: A data-centric trust pipeline: an empirical framework for trustworthy AI in sensitive domains
summary: This article proposes a four-layer governance framework, the Data-Centric Trust Pipeline, that couples integrity validation, fairness auditing, synthetic-data generation, and provenance recording, implemented in open-source Python and exercised on the Adult Census Income and COMPAS fairness benchmarks. The empirical evaluation runs 32 dataset-generator-seed configurations spanning three synthesizer families—Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and TVAE—to test whether the pipeline's fairness audit detects distributional-synthesis harms. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of the three generator families whose outputs feed the fairness audit that is the paper's central empirical claim.

title: SD-CGAN: Conditional Sinkhorn Divergence GAN for DDoS Anomaly Detection in IoT Networks
summary: This paper proposes SD-CGAN, a Conditional GAN framework enhanced with Sinkhorn Divergence for one-class anomaly detection of DDoS and zero-day attacks in IoT edge networks, trained on the CICDDoS2019 dataset. To address severe class imbalance in the exploitative attack subsets, the authors apply CTGAN to generate realistic minority-class synthetic flows, which are merged into the training set before the Sinkhorn-Divergence-optimized generator is trained on benign traffic. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional sampling are run as the data-augmentation stage feeding the whole detection pipeline, but the anomaly detector itself is SD-CGAN's own architecture.
evidence: "To mitigate class imbalance, we used CTGAN [6], a generative model tailored for mixed-type tabular data. CTGAN applies mode-specific normalization for continuous features and log-frequency sampling for categorical conditioning."
needs: Not fully clear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or a custom reimplementation was run; no import/package name or constructor parameters given, though the described mechanics (mode-specific normalization, log-frequency sampling) match the original CTGAN design closely.

title: CGDGMDA-Net: discovering microbe-disease and drug associations through CTGAN and graph-based deep learning
summary: This paper proposes CGDGMDA-Net, a computational method that pairs synthetic data generation with graph-based deep learning to predict associations among microbes, diseases, and drugs, addressing the scarcity of large curated microbial datasets. CTGAN is used as a data-augmentation step to expand the training data before the graph-based association-prediction models are applied. SDV's CTGAN component supplies the synthetic augmentation data underpinning this predictive pipeline.

title: The challenge of data scarcity and imbalanced classes in radiomics performance
summary: This paper studies how progressive data scarcity and class imbalance, individually and jointly, degrade the performance of radiomics-based machine learning models across three clinical imaging datasets (prostate cancer, glioblastoma, lung nodules). It evaluates several ML models and mitigation strategies, using state-of-the-art sampling techniques for imbalance and Tabular Variational Autoencoders for data scarcity. TVAE, the tabular variational autoencoder introduced in the CTGAN paper, is run as one of the mitigation techniques used to synthetically augment the scarce radiomics training data.
